I sat down on my aunt Reba's attic floor last Saturday and I couldn't get back up.
I don't mean I hurt myself. I didn't fall. I sat down criss cross like I was 8 years old to sort through a stack of shoeboxes, and 20 minutes later when I tried to stand my knees wouldn't lift me. My legs felt like wet cement. My arms had nothing in them. I ended up rolling onto my hip and using her old cedar chest to pull myself up, and I stood there breathing like I'd run to the mailbox and back.
I'm 54 years old.
My aunt was still driving to the beauty shop at 74 to get her hair set. And here I am with cement legs on an attic floor because I sat down for 20 minutes.
My name is LaWanda. I live in Meridian, Mississippi, about 15 minutes from where I grew up in a house on 34th Avenue where my grandmother taught me to snap green beans on the front porch. I work as an aide at Poplar Springs Elementary and I have been there for 19 years. I know every kindergartener in that building by name. I have wiped more noses and tied more shoelaces than any woman my age should be legally required to.
I am also tired all the time.
Not sleepy tired. Not the kind of tired you fix with a nap. I'm the kind of tired wh…
search.link_title: Feel Like Yourself Again "This actually worked, thank you so much." - Emily T.

I sat down on my aunt Reba's attic floor last Saturday and I couldn't get back up.
I don't mean I hurt myself. I didn't fall. I sat down criss cross like I was 8 years old to sort through a stack of shoeboxes, and 20 minutes later when I tried to stand my knees wouldn't lift me. My legs felt like wet cement. My arms had nothing in them. I ended up rolling onto my hip and using her old cedar chest to pull myself up, and I stood there breathing like I'd run to the mailbox and back.
I'm 54 years old.
My aunt was still driving to the beauty shop at 74 to get her hair set. And here I am with cement legs on an attic floor because I sat down for 20 minutes.
My name is LaWanda. I live in Meridian, Mississippi, about 15 minutes from where I grew up in a house on 34th Avenue where my grandmother taught me to snap green beans on the front porch. I work as an aide at Poplar Springs Elementary and I have been there for 19 years. I know every kindergartener in that building by name. I have wiped more noses and tied more shoelaces than any woman my age should be legally required to.
I am also tired all the time.
Not sleepy tired. Not the kind of tired you fix with a nap. I'm the kind of tired wh…

Grace came by and finished it for me. She didn't say anything but I could tell she knew. April 22, 1995. Tired. Tired. Tired. Woke up tired. Went to bed tired. Napped in between and woke up tired again. What is this. May 11, 1995. Ezra Sr. brought me groceries because I couldn't get to the store. He is a good boy. I don't want to be the aunt who needs groceries brought. Ezra Sr. That was my husband's father, who used to drive Reba around when she wasn't feeling up to it. I forgot he did that for her. I sat in that attic and I read her journal from 30 years ago and I could have been reading my own diary if I kept one. The same tiredness. The same doctor's visits with the same nothing answer. The same slow shrinking of her life, one canceled plan at a time. I read 15 more pages of it and I felt like somebody had reached into my chest and squeezed.
